Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the chase! The umpires have stepped on the green turf and so have the players. Will Malajczuk and Nitesh Samuel will be Australia Under-19's usual openers. Rasith Nimsara will have the new ball in hand with a slip in place. Lets play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

So 59 is the target for Australia Under-19 to get their third win in the group stage. It seems like an easy job for the batters of the side, but we have seen miracles happen in this sport. So take a break, refill your snacks as the second inning will commense in sometime.

Sri Lanka's highest partnership in the inning was just 12 runs and Chamika Heentigala is the player who scored the most in their camp. This simply summarises how the inning when for them. By the end of the inning, William Byrom got his fifer, Charles Lachmund and Kasey Barton bagged two each and Hayden Schiller chipped in for one.

Sri Lanka Under-19 just could not get going at all. They lost both their openers in the third over of the game and it was none other than Charles Lachmund who picked both the wickets. The wickets then just tumbled one by one, and William Byrom then stepped up to get rid of the entire top and middle-order batters of Sri Lanka. The Lankan camp was simply outplayed by their opposition. They tried to get a hold on the wicket by not playing big shots, but the lines and lengths of the bowlers were so tight that the Lankan batters couldn't restrict the Aussies from picking wickets.

Undoubtedly, the best bowling performance of this World Cup so far! Australia Under-19 have just dismantled Sri Lanka Under-19 here. Their plan started to work the moment they opted to bowl first. At the time of toss, their skipper, Oliver Peake, said that the best way to counter the Lankan batters is to attack them with pacers, and oh boy, they have done it outstandingly well. Special credit to William Byrom for getting his FIVE-FER, and the moment will surely stay forever with him.

OUT! TAKEN! FIVE-FER FOR BYROM! He bowls fuller, just outside off. Kugathas Mathulan lunges forward and attempts to drive at this half-volley delivery, but ends up slicing it uppishly and straight to the cover-point fielder. Steven Hogan doesn't really have to move as he just lifts his arm and pouches the catch over his head. After picking the wicket, Byrom is surrounded by his teammates, who pat him on the back and congratulate him on taking five wickets. Sri Lanka Under-19 are bundled out for 58.

Commentary.Howout: c Oliver Peake b Charles Lachmund
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, OUT! c Oliver Peake b Charles Lachmund.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Dimantha Mahavithana cuts it away towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Almost goes through! Charles Lachmund bowls another excellent yorker, on middle, swings inward in the air. Dulnith Sigera just about gets his bat time in time as it goes off the inner half of the bat through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Charles Lachmund to Dulnith Sigera, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dulnith Sigera walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! LBW! Charles Lachmund draws first blood and he deserves this wicket for the way he has bowled so far. This is full again, but on middle, attacks the stumps, angling in a bit. Viran Chamuditha gets stuck in his crease to clip it to the leg side but misses the line of the ball as his head falls and gets hit on the front pad right in front of the stumps. There is a big shout for LBW, and the finger goes up this time. Chamuditha walks back for 1 off 7, and Sri Lanka Under-19 are 2/1.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Charles Lachmund to Viran Chamuditha, OUT! lbw b Charles Lachmund.

Commentary.Commentary: Much fuller and around off, shaping away again, Viran Chamuditha has a waft at it but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Charles Lachmund to Viran Chamuditha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Errs in line and lands this on a hard length but way down the leg side, angling further into the leg side. Viran Chamuditha lets it go. Alex Lee Young, the keeper, dives to his right and grabs it with his outstretched right glove. Excellent take!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Charles Lachmund to Viran Chamuditha, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Charles Lachmund comes around the wicket, nails the yorker, on off, shapin away in the air, Viran Chamuditha digs it out well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Charles Lachmund to Viran Chamuditha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the length hard and around off, gets some extra bounce, Dimantha Mahavithana dabs it down towards point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: William Byrom to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and on off, Dimantha Mahavithana rides the bounce well and pats it down towards short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: William Byrom to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka Under-19 are finally underway after 10 balls! Good length and around leg, Viran Chamuditha flicks it through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: William Byrom to Viran Chamuditha, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Viran Chamuditha stabs it out to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: William Byrom to Viran Chamuditha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on middle, shaping in this time, Viran Chamuditha knocks it down the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: William Byrom to Viran Chamuditha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: William Byrom begins with a low full toss, around off, Viran Chamuditha looks to drive it away but gets it from the toe-end as it goes on the bounce to second slip.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: William Byrom to Viran Chamuditha, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: William Byrom to take the other new ball.
Short of a length and just outside off, Dimantha Mahavithana slashes hard at it but fails to connect. A maiden to start from Charles Lachmund!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up and on middle and leg, Dimantha Mahavithana gets behind the line of it and blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A massive shout for LBW, but turned down! Charles Lachmund serves this full and on middle, shaping in sharply. Dimantha Mahavithana looks to clip it across the line but misses and gets hit on the pads. Probably just going down the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Right in the blockhole, outside off, shapes in late, Dimantha Mahavithana leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! Back of a length and around off, takes off this time, Dimantha Mahavithana tries to cut it away but misses due to the extra bounce. A lot of 'Oos and Aas' in the slip cordon and the Aussies are putting the batter under pressure.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A beauty to start with! Charles Lachmund starts with a good-length delivery, on the fifth stump line, straightens off the deck. Dimantha Mahavithana has a tentative poke at it but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Charles Lachmund to Dimantha Mahavithana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! It is a clash between two unbeaten sides, but after this, only one will keep that record.  We can see the Aussies in a huddle before they spread out and take the fielding positions. Dimantha Mahavithana and Viran Chamuditha are the two openers for Sri Lanka Under-19. Charles Lachmund has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Two slips in place. Let's play...

Not far away from the start of the game, but before that, the players are walking out to the middle and lining up for their respective national anthems. It will be Australia's followed by that of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Alan Wilkins is pitchside. He says that it is another scorching day here and the sun is blazing down. Niall O'Brien joins him and says that the shorter square boundary is 61 meters, and the wind is blowing to that side as well. Adds that there are some indentations on the pitch as the heat is having it's affect. Reckons that the spinners will have a big say in this game.

Vimath Dinsara, the captain of Sri Lanka Under-19, says that they would have batted first anyway. Adds that they have a good, balanced side and are confident about this game. Says that Australia Under-19 are a strong side but they can challenge them.

Oliver Peake, the skipper of Australia Under-19, says that they have chased in the first two games and will look to continue with that intent. Adds that it looks like a good wicket and they will want to utilise the conditions early on. Informs that they have made three changes and are going with a pace-heavy attack. Says that they think that the Sri Lankan batters play spin very well, so they think pace is the best way to attack them.

Sri Lanka Under-19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Dimantha Mahavithana, Viran Chamuditha, Dulnith Sigera, Vimath Dinsara (C), Kavija Gamage, Chamika Heentigala, Adam Hilmy (WK), Sethmika Seneviratne, Rasith Nimsara, Kugathas Mathulan, Vigneshwaran Akash.

Australia Under-19 (Playing XI) - Will Malajczuk, Nitesh Samuel, Steven Hogan, Oliver Peake (C), Alex Lee Young (WK) (In place of Thomas Hogan), Jayden Draper, Aryan Sharma, Hayden Schiller (In place of Naden Cooray), Kasey Barton, William Byrom, Charles Lachmund (In place of Ben Gordon).
Australia Under-19 have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

Australia, the four times champions, are hot on the Lanka's heels, occupying second place in Group A with four points and a slight inferior net run rate than their opposition. The young Aussies have also rewritten the record books, with opening batter Will Malajczuk smashing the fastest century in U19 World Cup history, reaching his ton in just 51 balls against Japan. Malajczuk has been well-supported at the top by Nitesh Samuel, with back-to-back fifties. On the bowling front, Naden Cooray has proven to be a vital asset, recently picking up three wickets to stifle the Japanese middle order, while William Byrom and Charles Lachmund have looked threatening as well. With both sides boasting in-form power hitters and disciplined bowling attacks, this match promises to be one of the most competitive fixtures of the group stage. Stay tuned for toss and further updates.

Sri Lanka has been in sensational form, currently sitting at the top of the Group A points table with four points from two matches and a superior net run rate. Their campaign has been defined by record-breaking individual performances, most notably from opener Viran Chamuditha, who scripted history by scoring 192 against Japan, which is the the highest individual score in the history of the U19 World Cup. Chamuditha also shared a world-record opening partnership of 328 runs with Dimantha Mahavithana, who contributed a century of his own. In their second outing against Ireland, skipper Vimath Dinsara led from the front with a match-winning 95, while Dulnith Sigera dismantled the opposition with an exceptional bowling spell of 4/19. So Sri Lanka will be keen to convert this momentum into another complete performance in this World Cup and try to take on the defending champions.

Ladies and Gentlemen, a very warm welcome to everyone joining us for the build up of the coverage of Match 23 in the 2026 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup, an exciting Group A encounter between Sri Lanka Under-19 and Australia Under-19. This high-stakes clash is taking place at the Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek, where both teams are looking to maintain their dominant form in the tournament. As the sixteenth edition of the biennial showpiece, this match brings together two of the competition's strongest contenders in a battle for supremacy at the top of the table.
... MATCH DAY ...

As the ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2026 enters its critical final phase of the group stages, Match 23 brings us a heavyweight clash that could decide the hierarchy of Group A. The Namibia Cricket Ground in Windhoek is all set to host a battle of the unbeatens - defending champions Australia U19 going up against a surging Sri Lanka U19. With both teams already securing a foothold for the Super Six stage, this match is about more than just points. It’s about momentum, finishing top of the group and carrying maximum points forward. The defending champions have played like a team that knows how to win. Led by Oliver Peake, one of the heroes of the 2024 final, Australia’s brand of cricket has been ruthless. Their top order has been prolific, with Will Malajczuk recently smashing a sublime century and Nitesh Samuel providing consistent, explosive starts. What makes this Australian side unique is its diversity and bundles of local talent and for someone like Samuel, who is of Sri Lankan heritage, this game will add another layer of personal intensity.Sri Lanka has emerged as the dark horse of the tournament. Under Vimath Dinsara, the Lankans have showcased a balanced attack that thrives on Windhoek's surfaces. Their batting has found reliability in Dimantha Mahavithana, while the bowling unit, led by the pace of Vigneshwaran Akash, has been experts at strangling the run rate in the middle overs. For Sri Lanka, this match is a litmus test. Can they handle the high-velocity Australian pace attack, or will they be overwhelmed by the stage?While Australia enters as favorites based on their defending champion status and clinical top-order form, Sri Lanka’s spin variety and middle-order resilience make them a dangerous opponent. If the Sri Lankan spinners can extract grip from the Windhoek surface, the Australian middle order, which hasn't been under any pressure yet, could find themselves in uncharted waters. Who do you think will come out on top and clinch top spot in Group A?
